subject.title: [Feature]: Per-session activity state (busy/idle + awaiting_user, awaiting_subagent) via gateway API + WS statechange

question: Should OpenClaw add a gateway-owned `sessions.activity.get/list` plus `sessions.activity.statechange` contract now, and what minimal runtimeActivity/attention/children semantics belong in v1?
rationale: This defines a durable public Gateway/session API used by Control UI, CLI, external tools, and multi-agent workflows; source inspection shows no current equivalent, but the exact state model and persistence/reconnect semantics need maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Approve a narrow v1 activity contract
options.body: Define the smallest public API that covers busy/idle, explicit attention states, monotonic versions, stale-run handling, and reconnect resync, then route open PRs/follow-ups to that contract.

options.title: Limit to existing sessions.list/status projections
options.body: Keep the current row-level `hasActiveRun`/status approach and close or redirect broader activity API work as out of scope for now.

options.title: Defer until dashboard roadmap settles
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical design placeholder while dashboard/activity widget work validates the consumer shape first.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow v1 activity contract
recommendation.body: Define the smallest public API that covers busy/idle, explicit attention states, monotonic versions, stale-run handling, and reconnect resync, then route open PRs/follow-ups to that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is currently assigned to `vincentkoc`, making them the clearest live routing owner for the product/API decision despite shared code ownership.
